Exposure to smoke, pollution, chemical fumes, and gas leaks can irritate the eyes and affect daily comfort.

Best Eye Specialist for Retina Problems | ASG Eye Hospital

The retina plays a vital role in vision, yet many retinal conditions develop silently and may not show symptoms until significant damage has occurred. Early diagnosis by a retina specialist can help protect vision and improve treatment outcomes.

Warning signs that need immediate attention:

• Sudden flashes of light
• New or increasing floaters
• Blurred or distorted vision
• A dark curtain or shadow in vision
• Difficulty reading or recognising faces
• Sudden vision loss

Common retina disorders include diabetic retinopathy, retinal detachment, macular degeneration, macular holes, and retinal tears. Many of these conditions respond better when diagnosed and treated early.

At ASG Eye Hospital, advanced retinal imaging and modern diagnostic technology help specialists detect retinal problems accurately and recommend the most appropriate retina treatment.

Available treatment options may include:

• Retinal laser treatment
• Intravitreal injections
• Vitrectomy surgery
• Retinal detachment repair
• Ongoing retinal monitoring

Delaying treatment can increase the risk of permanent vision loss. If you notice any sudden changes in your eyesight, seeking prompt evaluation from a qualified retina specialist is essential.

Book your retina consultation at ASG Eye Hospital today and take the first step toward protecting your vision.

Diabetes can affect your eyesight without obvious warning signs. Many people with diabetic eye disease experience no symptoms until retinal damage has already begun. Regular eye examinations are essential for protecting long-term vision.

Common symptoms to watch for include:

• Blurred or fluctuating vision
• Floaters or dark spots
• Difficulty reading
• Distorted vision
• Poor night vision
• Sudden vision changes

One of the most common diabetes-related eye conditions is diabetic retinopathy, which affects the blood vessels in the retina. Early detection through retinal screening can help prevent serious vision complications.

Protect your eye health by:

• Maintaining healthy blood sugar levels
• Monitoring blood pressure regularly
• Taking medications as prescribed
• Staying physically active

• Scheduling regular eye check-ups

He also said he could do the test if I still felt like but it’s not needed.

Obviously not convinced I told him I would still like to do the eye swab test. He was angry that I did not listen to his advice and still requested the test to be done. The skin around my eyes, due to the prolonged infection was already dry and cracking. Dr. Nikunj was extremely passive aggressive and did not consider being gentle.

*His ego was hurt and he kept trying to stand his ground that the swab test is not needed and in anger he opened my eye so roughly to do the swab test that the skin at the corner of the eye tore and I WAS BLEEDING!*

Being a spiritual healer, my body sensed a kind of abuse and insensitivity that I cannot forget to this date.

And it goes without saying HIS DIAGNOSIS WAS ABSOLUTELY INCORRECT. The swab test results came in perfectly fine (contrary to what he had said) and I was detected with a severe staphylococcus aureus infection! THANKS TO THE SWAB TEST THAT HE DIDNT THINK WAS IMPORTANT but I knew I needed it.

Doctors like him need to understand that patients can know their bodies well and KNOW when something is not right!

Not only this, he charged me twice (once when I asked if he can do the test and he said no. And second when I was still insisted to do the test and he did it in anger!). Absolutely incorrigible and a nightmare of an experience!

featured_reviews.review_text:
I had an unpleasant experience with Dr Jatin Ashar. I visited with my father to inquire about getting lens, but the doctor insisted on LASIK surgery instead. When my father asked if the procedure was covered under CGHS, the doctor responded rudely and irritably, saying, "Har cheez CGHS ke andar nahi aata" (Not everything comes under CGHS). When my father mentioned that we could not afford the surgery, the doctor dismissed us immediately.

The doctor’s rude and dismissive behaviour felt unprofessional and gave the impression that the focus was more on money than on providing patient care.

Edit -

Thank you for your response. I would like to clarify a few things further:

1. Regarding the insistence on surgery:
While I appreciate your clarification, the fact remains that my initial query was regarding lenses, not surgery. The suggestion of LASIK surgery was made without taking my actual concern into consideration, which felt like an insistence on a different treatment.

2. Conveying information about CGHS coverage:
I understand that you were sharing a fact about CGHS coverage. However, the way it was conveyed—specifically the eye-roll and the tone—felt rude and dismissive. A simple fact can be stated in a respectful and professional manner, without conveying irritation. My concern is not about the fact itself but the delivery.

3. Dismissing us after mentioning affordability:
When my father expressed that we could not afford the surgery, the immediate dismissal of us from the consultation felt unprofessional. Instead of discussing alternative options or even providing some guidance, we were effectively shown the door. This is what I meant by being dismissed.

4. False promises or commitments:
While I agree that false promises should not be made, professionalism involves handling all patients with respect and care, especially when they raise concerns. In our case, the conversation could have been handled with more patience and understanding, and alternatives could have been suggested instead of just ending the interaction.

5. Professionalism and respect:
I believe professionalism goes beyond just giving facts; it also includes how we make patients feel during consultations. In this instance, the interaction left us feeling dismissed rather than respected or valued as patients. A more considerate and understanding approach would have made a positive difference.

Edit 2 -

It’s quite surprising to see how delusional one can be. At no point did I claim that Dr Ashar discussed charges or financial solutions with us. My concern was about his dismissive attitude and the way he handled our query.

Firmness and being straight to the point are not the issues here. The problem is the lack of courtesy and professionalism displayed during the interaction. Rolling one’s eyes, speaking irritably, and dismissing patients when they express financial constraints are not examples of firmness—they are examples of rude behaviour.

If you are unwilling to acknowledge this, that’s your prerogative, but dismissing genuine concerns as a misunderstanding or misrepresentation reflects poorly on the ability to take accountability.

Lastly, your attempt to redirect me to a counsellor for further assistance misses the point entirely. This is not about needing financial advice or further treatment—it’s about the lack of respect shown to patients during a consultation.

Pediatric Ophthalmologist – Expert Eye Care for Children

From routine eye examinations to the treatment of squint (strabismus), lazy eye (amblyopia), refractive errors, congenital eye disorders, and pediatric cataracts, we offer personalized treatment plans tailored to your child's needs. Early diagnosis and timely treatment can help prevent long-term vision problems and support healthy visual development.

With increased use of smartphones, tablets, and computers, protecting children's vision has become more important than ever. Encourage regular screen breaks, maintain proper viewing distance, ensure good lighting during screen use, and promote outdoor activities to help reduce eye strain and support healthy visual development.

Parents should also watch for signs such as frequent eye rubbing, headaches, blurred vision, or difficulty focusing, as these may indicate underlying vision concerns. Regular eye check-ups can help detect problems early and ensure children maintain healthy eyesight as they grow.

Eye strain in children is becoming more common with increased screen time, less outdoor play, poor lighting, and long hours of reading or close-up work. Symptoms often include tired eyes, headaches, blurred vision, frequent eye rubbing, and difficulty concentrating.

Simple steps can make a big difference: encouraging regular screen breaks, keeping proper viewing distances, ensuring adequate lighting, and scheduling routine eye check-ups. Paying attention to early signs helps prevent discomfort and supports healthier vision development, giving children a stronger foundation for learning and growth.

My concern is simple: if the cataract was so complicated, why wasn’t this identified during diagnosis? We could have been referred earlier instead of going through a failed surgery and immense mental stress.

Dr. Mehta charged ₹30,000 for cataract removal (₹37,000 quoted including lens). Later, through another retina specialist (not the one recommended by him), we learned that the cataract was not fully removed and eye pressure was increasing. This was never clearly communicated to us despite multiple post-op visits.

We eventually consulted another specialist. The second surgery was successful without stitches, contradicting the earlier claim that a stitched lens was mandatory. My mother is now recovering well.

Due to the failed surgery, lack of transparency, and poor communication, Dr. Hiren Mehta has lost our trust. I would not recommend this clinic for eye surgeries. Please consider multiple opinions before proceeding.

Titan Eye+ at Krushal Shopping Complex (next to Shoppers Stop, Tilak Nagar, Chembur) has zero parking and even less class.

To suggest a customer would commute via bicycle for premium eyewear is as delusional as their lack of basic infrastructure.

Save yourself the fine and the headache—stick to a mall where they actually value your patronage and your time.
